Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Passwordless sudo rule dropped into /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma privilege escalation) · [LLM] Security vendor domain blackhole written to /etc/hosts from non-admin process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Bun runtime spawned via node→shell→bun chain from npm install (Miasma dropper) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping (Miasma payload) · [LLM] Cloud IMDS credential harvesting from node/bun process on CI runner · [LLM] Public GitHub repo creation matching Miasma 'adjective-creature-N' exfil pattern · [LLM] Worm-injected .github/setup.js commit with 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]' message · [LLM] Destructive 'rm -rf ~' or Miasma honeytoken tripwire from node/bun process tree · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Bun runtime spawned via node→shell→bun chain from npm install (Miasma dropper) AIInstallation High
Hunts the signature process tree of the Red Hat npm Miasma campaign: a node.js process spawning a shell that spawns the Bun runtime, typically from npm preinstall hooks. This is the exact anti-Node-monitoring evasion chain the article identifies for the 4.29 MB index.js dropper. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact statement: 'creating an unusual process chain (node → shell → bun → payload) designed to evade Node-focused monitoring.' The Bun runtime is downloaded to a temp path before execution, and bun is not a standard CI runner tool — the parent-of-parent being node/npm in a preinstall context is article-specific.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate developer running 'bun run' inside their local project that was bootstrapped via npm install scripts
  • CI pipelines that have intentionally adopted Bun as their JS runtime (e.g. via 'bun install' wrapper scripts that call node first)
  • Bun official installer (curl bun.sh/install | bash) executed by an admin
  • Internal monorepo tooling that proxies node through shell wrappers to invoke bun
  • Docker buildkit layers running bun in /tmp for ephemeral compile steps
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "bun-baseline-pipeline" or InitiatingProcessParentCommandLine has "bun-baseline-pipeline")
| where not (DeviceName has "buildkit" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "docker-buildkit")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: pivot on InitiatingProcessParentCommandLine for the npm package name and version; correlate with DeviceFileEvents for the index.js write that immediately preceded execution — cross-check the SHA256 against 7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655 / b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966. 2. CONTAIN: isolate the runner/dev host, revoke its GitHub Actions OIDC tokens and any npm publish PATs scoped to the user, rotate cloud IMDS-reachable role credentials. 3. HUNT: pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound bun.sh downloads and api.github.com posts from the same DeviceId, and to CloudAppEvents for repo creation under the user's GitHub account in the next 60 minutes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun", "bun.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm","npm-cli.js","yarn","pnpm")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall","npm install","index.js")
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/home/runner/" or FolderPath has "/.bun/" or FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\" or FolderPath has "/var/folders/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
    ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
    GrandparentFile = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "bun.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "sh" or ParentProcessName endswith "bash" or ParentProcessName endswith "cmd.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "powershell.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node","npm","preinstall","index.js")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/","/home/runner/","/.bun/",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\","/var/folders/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun Runtime Spawned by Node Shell Chain (Miasma npm Dropper)
id: a3f9d8e2-7b41-4c5a-9e2d-1f8b6c3a9d77
description: Detects the node → shell → bun process chain characteristic of the Red Hat npm Miasma supply chain campaign, where a preinstall hook executes a 4.29 MB index.js dropper that downloads and detonates the Bun runtime.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1546.016
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bun'
      - '/bun.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  selection_grandparent_or_path:
    - ParentCommandLine|contains:
        - 'node'
        - 'npm'
        - 'preinstall'
        - 'index.js'
    - Image|contains:
        - '/tmp/'
        - '/home/runner/'
        - '/.bun/'
        - '\Temp\'
        - '/var/folders/'
  condition: selection_image and selection_parent and selection_grandparent_or_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer use of Bun in npm scripts (rare in CI baseline)
  - Bun installer running interactively (curl https://bun.sh/install | bash)
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:bun OR @process.name:bun.exe OR @Image:(*\bun OR *\bun.exe OR */bun OR */bun.exe)) (@process.parent.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR zsh OR cmd.exe OR powershell.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\sh OR *\bash OR *\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe)) (@process.command_line:(*node* OR *npm* OR *preinstall* OR *index.js*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*node* OR *npm* OR *preinstall* OR *index.js*)) (@process.executable.path:(*/tmp/* OR */home/runner/* OR */.bun/* OR */var/folders/*) OR @Image:(*\Temp\* OR */tmp/* OR */.bun/*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/bun(\.exe)?$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(sh|bash|dash|zsh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe)$/i
| regex("(node|npm|preinstall|index\\.js)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| regex("(\/tmp\/|\/home\/runner\/|\.bun\/|\\\\Temp\\\\|\/var\/folders\/)", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, ParentCommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="bun" OR Processes.process_name="bun.exe") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="dash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="zsh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="powershell.exe") AND (Processes.parent_process="*node*" OR Processes.parent_process="*npm*" OR Processes.parent_process="*preinstall*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="bun" OR Processes.process_name="bun.exe") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="dash" OR Processes.parent_process_name="zsh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="cmd.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="powershell.exe") AND (Processes.parent_process="*node*" OR Processes.parent_process="*npm*" OR Processes.parent_process="*preinstall*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping (Miasma payload) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma payload's runtime-secret theft technique: scanning /proc/<pid>/cmdline for 'Runner.Worker' to locate the GitHub Actions worker PID, then extracting masked Actions secrets from process memory via a distinctive grep regex for '"isSecret":true' JSON tokens. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim code block: 'findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux', the exact extraction regex 'grep -aoE \'"[^"]+":{"value":"[^"]*","isSecret":true}\'', and the /proc/<pid>/cmdline scan strategy. These strings have no legitimate occurrence outside this campaign and the article explicitly cites them as the runner-memory exfiltration mechanism.
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.005 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • GitHub Actions runner internal diagnostic scripts walking /proc (parent should be Runner.Listener)
  • Security tooling like osquery or auditbeat scanning /proc/<pid>/cmdline for inventory
  • SOC IR scripts performing memory triage that grep for 'isSecret' patterns
  • Legitimate Docker/Kubernetes diagnostic containers scanning process tree on the runner
  • Custom CI debug steps echoing masked secrets to logs (the regex marker would appear in logs but not in process args)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !endswith "Runner.Listener"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("osqueryd","auditbeat","falcon-sensor")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: capture the full process tree and confirm parent is NOT Runner.Listener / actions.runner.worker; pull the cmdline and check for the exact 'isSecret' regex which has no legitimate runtime use. 2. CONTAIN: terminate the offending PID, freeze the runner VM/container, rotate ALL secrets exposed to ANY workflow run on that runner within the last 30 days (GitHub org/repo/env secrets, OIDC-trusted cloud roles). 3. HUNT: pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound api.github.com PUT/POST traffic from the runner immediately after the scrape, and to GitHub audit logs for unexpected repo creation under the maintainer account.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker", "findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux", "\"isSecret\":true")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "grep" and ProcessCommandLine has "-aoE" and ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "cmdline")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "cmdline" and ProcessCommandLine has "tr -d")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("runner-worker","Runner.Listener","actions.runner")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
    InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker", "findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux", "\"isSecret\":true")
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "grep" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-aoE" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "cmdline")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "Runner.Listener"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GitHub Actions Runner.Worker Memory Scraping (Miasma)
id: 5e7c2d91-3b48-4a67-bc1e-9d4f7a8e6c52
description: Detects scraping of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process memory for masked secrets, using the regex pattern '"isSecret":true' on /proc/<pid>/cmdline reads. Specific to the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing campaign.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1003
  - attack.t1552.005
  - attack.t1057
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_marker:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Runner.Worker'
      - 'findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux'
      - '"isSecret":true'
  selection_grep_regex:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'grep'
      - '-aoE'
      - '/proc/'
      - 'cmdline'
  condition: selection_marker or selection_grep_regex
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate GitHub Actions runner self-diagnostics (verify ParentImage is Runner.Listener)
  - SOC forensics tooling scanning /proc for incident response
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*Runner.Worker* OR *findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux* OR *\"isSecret\":true*) OR (@process.command_line:*grep* AND @process.command_line:*\-aoE* AND @process.command_line:*\/proc\/* AND @process.command_line:*cmdline*)) -@process.executable.path:*Runner.Listener*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("(Runner\\.Worker|findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux|\"isSecret\":true)", field=CommandLine)
   OR (regex("grep", field=CommandLine) | regex("-aoE", field=CommandLine) | regex("/proc/", field=CommandLine) | regex("cmdline", field=CommandLine))
| ParentBaseFileName!=/Runner\.Listener/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*Runner.Worker*" OR Processes.process="*findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux*" OR Processes.process="*\"isSecret\":true*" OR (Processes.process="*grep*" AND Processes.process="*-aoE*" AND Processes.process="*/proc/*" AND Processes.process="*cmdline*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*Runner.Worker*" OR Processes.process="*findRunnerWorkerPIDLinux*" OR Processes.process="*\"isSecret\":true*" OR (Processes.process="*grep*" AND Processes.process="*-aoE*" AND Processes.process="*/proc/*" AND Processes.process="*cmdline*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Cloud IMDS credential harvesting from node/bun process on CI runner AIActions on Objectives High
Detects short-lived node or bun processes contacting the AWS/Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) or GCP metadata service (metadata.google.internal) — the Miasma payload's mechanism for stealing instance role credentials, Azure IMDS OAuth2 tokens, and GCP service-account tokens from CI runners. Rationale: Anchored on the article's credential-theft section listing exact endpoints: 'IMDS (169.254.169.254)', 'metadata.google.internal service-account tokens', and 'IMDS OAuth2 tokens for management.azure.com, graph.microsoft.com, and Key Vault (*.vault.azure.net)'. Node/bun calling IMDS from a CI runner is the article's specific behavior — the article notes Linux CI runners as the primary target.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1528 T1552.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS SDK v3 in Node.js apps legitimately calling IMDS to resolve instance role credentials on EC2
  • Bun-based Lambda runtime adapters or Vercel/Netlify Edge functions querying their host metadata
  • Kubernetes IRSA workloads where the SDK contacts the IMDS proxy
  • Azure Functions custom containers using @azure/identity DefaultAzureCredential
  • GCP Cloud Run / GKE workloads using google-auth-library to resolve service-account credentials
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("aws-sdk","@azure/identity","google-auth-library")
| where DeviceName !startswith "baseline-sdk-app"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: pivot on InitiatingProcessCommandLine to confirm the node/bun process is not a known SDK-using app (check against ServiceNow CMDB inventory); look for parent process being npm/preinstall and IMDS calls within seconds of process start. 2. CONTAIN: rotate the IMDS-exposed role credentials on the affected host immediately (AWS: IAM revoke-active-sessions; Azure: revoke managed identity tokens; GCP: rotate service account key), then quarantine the host. 3. HUNT: in CloudTrail/AzureActivity/GCP audit, pivot on the leaked role principal for AssumeRole / API activity from non-instance IPs in the 24h after the call — a key Miasma exfil signal is the credentials being used from attacker infrastructure.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254" or RemoteUrl has_any ("metadata.google.internal", "169.254.169.254", "metadata.azure.com", ".vault.azure.net")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","bun","bun.exe")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(RemoteUrl), IPHits = make_set(RemoteIP), HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where HitCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254" or DstHostname has_any ("metadata.google.internal","metadata.azure.com",".vault.azure.net")
| where Url has_any ("node","bun") or DstHostname has_any ("metadata","vault.azure")
| summarize EndpointsHit = make_set(DstHostname), HitCount = count() by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by HitCount desc
title: Cloud IMDS Access by Node or Bun Process (Miasma Harvester)
id: 8b1c4e72-5d39-4f86-a2b1-7e3c9f5a4d18
description: Detects node or bun processes contacting cloud instance metadata endpoints (AWS IMDS 169.254.169.254, GCP metadata.google.internal, Azure IMDS, Key Vault) to harvest temporary cloud credentials. Specific to the Red Hat npm Miasma campaign on CI runners and developer hosts.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1552.005
  - attack.t1528
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/bun'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
  selection_dest:
    DestinationIp:
      - '169.254.169.254'
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'metadata.google.internal'
      - 'metadata.azure.com'
      - '.vault.azure.net'
  condition: selection_process and selection_dest
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Node.js apps using AWS SDK / Azure SDK that resolve IMDS for instance role credentials
  - Bun-based serverless adapters that intentionally call IMDS
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon OR cloudtrail) (@network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.host:(metadata.google.internal OR metadata.azure.com) OR @DestinationHostname:(metadata.google.internal OR *.vault.azure.net)) (@process.name:(node OR bun) OR @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\bun.exe OR */node OR */bun))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=DnsRequest)
| (RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" OR DomainName=/metadata\.(google\.internal|azure\.com)/i OR DomainName=/.*\.vault\.azure\.net$/i)
| ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|bun)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, bytes
| filter dstAddr = "169.254.169.254"
      and action = "ACCEPT"
| stats count(*) as imdsCalls, sum(bytes) as totalBytes by srcAddr, bin(5m)
| sort @timestamp desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="169.254.169.254" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="metadata.google.internal") AND (All_Traffic.process_name="node" OR All_Traffic.process_name="node.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="169.254.169.254" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="metadata.google.internal") AND (All_Traffic.process_name="node" OR All_Traffic.process_name="node.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun" OR All_Traffic.process_name="bun.exe") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Passwordless sudo rule dropped into /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma privilege escalation) AIExploitation High
Detects creation of files under /etc/sudoers.d containing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' (specifically the 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' string the Miasma payload writes), and the bind-mount-to-/mnt technique used to deposit the sudoers fragment. Sigma covers the process-create path; KQL covers both file-write and sudoers-validation chains. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact verbatim code block: "echo 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' > ... && chmod 0440 /mnt/runner" and "sudo -n true". The 'NOPASSWD:ALL' string combined with a /etc/sudoers.d or /mnt/ write target is the article-specific signature; this rule should not fire on legitimate config-mgmt because we filter on node/bun/shell parents.
ATT&CKT1548.003 T1098
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Chef/Puppet runs deploying CI runner sudoers fragments at provisioning time
  • Cloud-init bake scripts on AMI build that legitimately add 'runner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'
  • Packer / image-builder workflows constructing sudoers files during golden-image creation
  • Kubernetes self-hosted runner Helm charts that templatize sudoers.d entries
  • Manual sysadmin troubleshooting via 'visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/runner'
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible","chef-client","puppet-agent","cloud-init","packer","kubelet")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ansible","chef-client","puppet-agent","cloud-init","packer")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: confirm parent process is node/bun/sh and not ansible-playbook, chef-client, puppet, cloud-init, packer, or kubelet (legitimate deployers); the article-specific signal is the bind-mount via /mnt. 2. CONTAIN: remove the rogue sudoers fragment, terminate the offending process tree, freeze the runner instance and preserve disk for forensics, revoke any tokens cached in /home/runner/.config and /home/runner/work/_temp. 3. HUNT: pivot to subsequent 'sudo -n true' and 'sudo sh -c' invocations from the same AccountName, and to /etc/hosts writes for security-vendor blackholes (the follow-on Miasma defense-evasion step).
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (FolderPath startswith "/mnt/" and FileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","cp","mv","dd")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName_proc = InitiatingProcessFileName)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "NOPASSWD:ALL"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/sudoers.d","/mnt/","sudoers")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
       or (TargetFilePath startswith "/mnt/" and TargetFileName has_any ("runner","sudoers"))
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Passwordless Sudo Rule Drop via /etc/sudoers.d (Miasma)
id: c4f2a51d-86b3-4c19-9e7a-2d8b6f3c4a91
description: Detects the Miasma payload writing 'NOPASSWD:ALL' rules into /etc/sudoers.d (often via a bind-mount of /mnt), granting passwordless root to the runner/maintainer account.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:

Security vendor domain blackhole written to /etc/hosts from non-admin process AIExploitation High
Detects the Miasma payload's defense-evasion step where it pipes 'echo 127.0.0.1 <vendor>' through sudo to append to /etc/hosts, blackholing telemetry/update domains for installed security products. Anchored on /etc/hosts writes initiated by node/bun/shell processes. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim code block: 'sudo sh -c "echo \'127.0.0.1 <vendor>\' >> /etc/hosts"' under the Neutralize Security product monitoring comment. The combination of /etc/hosts + 127.0.0.1 + append from a node/bun/sh parent on a CI runner is highly article-specific.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1565.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dockerfile RUN steps editing /etc/hosts inside container build layers
  • Cloud-init / userdata adding loopback overrides for local services on VM bootstrap
  • Vagrant / minikube provisioners writing 127.0.0.1 entries for dev hostnames
  • Local dev sysadmins overriding production domains to point at staging
  • Kubernetes coredns config-test scripts editing /etc/hosts in a debug pod
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("docker build","buildkit","vagrant","minikube")
| where DeviceName !startswith "builder-" and DeviceName !startswith "packer-"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: capture the appended /etc/hosts line(s); cross-reference the blackholed domain against your EDR/AV vendor's update/telemetry domain list (CrowdStrike, Defender, SentinelOne, Trend) — if the domain is a security product, treat as confirmed compromise. 2. CONTAIN: restore /etc/hosts from a known-good baseline, isolate the host, kill the node/bun parent tree, snapshot disk for forensics, and rotate any creds reachable from the host. 3. HUNT: pivot on InitiatingProcessFolderPath for the dropper script that issued the command, then DeviceProcessEvents for follow-on 'sudo -n true' validation and IMDS / GitHub API calls in the next 5 minutes.
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","sudo")
       or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath == "/etc/" and FileName == "hosts"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","tee","sudo")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, Source, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/etc/hosts"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has "127.0.0.1"
       and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (">>"," tee ","echo ")
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","sudo")
    | extend Source = "ProcessCreate"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFilePath == "/etc/hosts"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","tee")
    | extend Source = "FileWrite", ActingProcessCommandLine = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Source, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: /etc/hosts Blackhole Write from Node or Bun Process (Miasma Defense Evasion)
id: 7e3a1b94-c52f-4d68-b1ae-9f4d8c2e7b15
description: Detects the Miasma payload writing 127.0.0.1 entries to /etc/hosts (typically to blackhole security vendor update/telemetry domains) via a node/bun/shell pipeline using echo + sudo + redirect.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1565.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains: '/etc/hosts'
  selection_loopback:
    CommandLine|contains: '127.0.0.1'
  selection_write:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '>>'
      - ' tee '
      - 'echo '
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/bun'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sudo'
      - '/npm'
  condition: selection_target and selection_loopback and selection_write and selection_parent
falsepositives:
  - Container build steps adding loopback overrides in Dockerfile RUN
  - Internal IT scripts overriding DNS for staging environments
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*\/etc\/hosts* @process.command_line:*127.0.0.1* (@process.command_line:*\>\>* OR @process.command_line:*tee* OR @process.command_line:*echo*) (@process.parent.name:(node OR bun OR sh OR bash OR sudo OR npm) OR @ParentImage:(*\node OR *\bun OR *\sh OR *\bash))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("/etc/hosts", field=CommandLine)
| regex("127\\.0\\.0\\.1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(>>|\\stee\\s|echo\\s)", field=CommandLine)
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|bun|sh|bash|dash|sudo|npm)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/etc/hosts*" AND Processes.process="*127.0.0.1*" AND (Processes.process="*>>*" OR Processes.process="*tee*" OR Processes.process_name="echo") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/etc/hosts*" AND Processes.process="*127.0.0.1*" AND (Processes.process="*>>*" OR Processes.process="*tee*" OR Processes.process_name="echo") AND (Processes.parent_process_name="node" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bun" OR Processes.parent_process_name="sh" OR Processes.parent_process_name="bash") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Public GitHub repo creation matching Miasma 'adjective-creature-N' exfil pattern AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma exfiltration channel: creation of a public GitHub repository under a victim's account named with the adjective-creature-N convention and/or containing the 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' description, followed by commits to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json paths. Pivots on CloudAppEvents / GitHub audit logs. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 10 of the article: 'Creates a public repo in the victim’s GitHub account ("Miasma: The Spreading Blight") and commits stolen credential JSON to results/<timestamp>-<counter>.json' and the adjective-creature-<0-99999> naming convention called out in the kill-chain reconstruction. Both the regex name pattern and the 'Miasma' string have no legitimate use in this org's GitHub footprint.
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer creating a public repo for a personal toy project that happens to match adjective-creature-N (e.g. 'happy-otter-42') — visibility=public filter helps but is not exhaustive
  • GitHub default repo suggestion using fun random names (rare, normally takes 'fluffy-octopus' shape with 2 tokens, not 3 with a number)
  • Hackathon teams using a generated team-name + entry-number convention
  • Bot-driven repo creation by legitimate automation (filter on AccountDisplayName not being github-actions[bot])
  • Internal blue-team exercises planting decoy repos matching this pattern
Suppression filter
| where AccountDisplayName !has "[bot]"
| where Description !has_any ("hackathon","team-","toy-","playground")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: open the matched repo URL and inspect results/*.json contents — if present, treat as confirmed exfiltration; capture the file SHAs and the maintainer's PAT inventory. 2. CONTAIN: revoke ALL PATs and OIDC-trusted tokens for the maintainer account, force a GitHub session reset, delete the public repo (after preserving evidence), and disable the maintainer's npm publish rights until investigation completes. 3. HUNT: pivot on the maintainer account for additional repo creates, new .github/setup.js commits across owned repos, and any npm publishes within the same 24h — the worm tries to spread to all maintainer-owned packages.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("Create repository","RepositoryCreate","repo.create")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"
| where RepoName matches regex @"^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$"
   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight","The Spreading Blight")
   or RawEventData has "results/" and RawEventData has ".json"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, RepoName, Visibility, Description, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Pre-req: GitHub Enterprise audit log connector ingesting into a custom GitHubAudit_CL table, or using OfficeActivity for GitHub via Cloud App Security
let GitHubLogs = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has_any ("GitHub","github")
           or RecordType has "GitHub";
GitHubLogs
| where Operation has_any ("repo.create","RepositoryCreate","Create repository")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).visibility)
| extend Description = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).description)
| where Visibility =~ "public"
| where RepoName matches regex @"^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$"
   or Description has_any ("Miasma","Spreading Blight")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, RepoName, Visibility, Description, Operation
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:github @action:(repo.create OR RepositoryCreate) @repo.visibility:public (@repo.name:/^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{1,5}$/ OR @repo.description:(*Miasma* OR *"Spreading Blight"*))
CLOUD
`github_audit_log` action="repo.create" visibility="public" (repo="*-*-*" OR description="*Miasma*" OR description="*Spreading Blight*") | rex field=repo "^(?<adj>[a-z]+)-(?<creature>[a-z]+)-(?<idx>\d{1,5})$" | where isnotnull(idx) AND idx>=0 AND idx<=99999 | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, count by user, repo, description, visibility | sort - firstSeen
Worm-injected .github/setup.js commit with 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]' message AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the Miasma worm's lateral-movement technique: commits adding a .github/setup.js file via the GitHub Git Data API, authored as 'github-actions@github.com' with the verbatim message 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. These commits appear across non-protected branches in victim-owned repos and skip CI by design. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 11 of the kill-chain reconstruction: 'Hunt for commits adding .github/setup.js authored as github-actions@github.com with message chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. The exact file path, author email, and commit message are verbatim worm signatures with no legitimate corollary — Dependabot uses a different author identity and never adds setup.js.
ATT&CKT1080 T1195.002 T1098.004
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine github-actions bot updating workflow files (would NOT touch .github/setup.js)
  • Internal CI automation re-using the github-actions identity for housekeeping commits with similar message wording
  • Dependabot rebase commits (these author as dependabot[bot], not github-actions)
  • Repo templates that ship with .github/setup.js as a legitimate bootstrap script
  • Developers manually committing as the github-actions identity for testing (rare — requires PAT misuse)
Suppression filter
| where ObjectName !endswith "-template" and ObjectName !contains "boilerplate"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: inspect the .github/setup.js diff — if it contains obfuscated JS, eval(), Buffer.from(base64), or fetch to api.github.com / bun.sh, treat as confirmed worm injection. 2. CONTAIN: revoke the OIDC token / PAT that authored the commit, revert the commit across ALL affected repos (use the GitHub API to delete or revert the matching SHA), force-rotate the maintainer's GitHub session, audit npm publishes signed by exchanged OIDC tokens from this maintainer in the last 7 days. 3. HUNT: enumerate ALL repos owned by the maintainer for additional .github/setup.js files or matching commit messages, and check Sigstore/Rekor transparency log for unexpected SLSA provenance entries against the maintainer's npm packages.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.push","push","PushCommit","Push")
| extend Files = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).added)
| extend Message = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).message)
| extend AuthorEmail = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).author_email)
| where Files has ".github/setup.js"
   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, ObjectName, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, IPAddress, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
let GitHubLogs = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where OfficeWorkload has "GitHub" or RecordType has "GitHub";
GitHubLogs
| where Operation has_any ("git.push","push","PushCommit")
| extend Files = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).added)
| extend Message = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).message)
| extend AuthorEmail = tostring(parse_json(tostring(EventData)).author_email)
| where Files has ".github/setup.js"
   or (Message =~ "chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" and AuthorEmail =~ "github-actions@github.com")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ObjectId, Files, Message, AuthorEmail, ClientIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Worm .github/setup.js Injection Commit
id: 9d1f5c83-2a47-4b96-8e1c-3f7a8b9d6e21
description: Detects commits that add .github/setup.js with the Miasma worm's signature author 'github-actions@github.com' and message 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'. This is the worm's mechanism to spread laterally across victim-owned GitHub repos via the Git Data API.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1080
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  product: github
  service: audit
detection:
  selection_file:
    added_files|contains: '.github/setup.js'
  selection_author_msg:
    commit_author_email: 'github-actions@github.com'
    commit_message: 'chore: update dependencies [skip ci]'
  condition: selection_file or selection_author_msg
falsepositives:
  - Genuine Dependabot or Renovate bot commits (but those use dependabot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com, not github-actions@github.com, and don't add .github/setup.js)
  - Internal automation legitimately authoring as github-actions@github.com to update workflows
level: high
source:github @action:(git.push OR push OR PushCommit) (@commit.added:*.github\/setup.js* OR (@commit.author.email:github-actions@github.com AND @commit.message:"chore: update dependencies [skip ci]"))
CLOUD
`github_audit_log` (action="git.push" OR action="push") (commit_message="chore: update dependencies [skip ci]" OR added_files="*.github/setup.js*") | rex max_match=1 field=added_files "(?<setupjs>\.github/setup\.js)" | where isnotnull(setupjs) OR (commit_author_email="github-actions@github.com" AND commit_message="chore: update dependencies [skip ci]") | stats min(_time) as firstSeen, dc(repo) as repoCount, values(repo) as repos by user, commit_author_email | sort - firstSeen
Destructive 'rm -rf ~' or Miasma honeytoken tripwire from node/bun process tree AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Miasma destructive fail-safe: 'rm -rf ~/' / 'rm -rf ~/Documents' invoked by a node or bun process tree (often after the planted honeytoken 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' is touched). Also directly matches the honeytoken string in any process command line or file content. Rationale: Anchored on Phase 12 of the kill-chain reconstruction: the verbatim honeytoken string 'IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner' and the destructive commands 'rm -rf ~/' and 'rm -rf ~/Documents'. The honeytoken string is unique to this campaign with zero legitimate use; the rm-rf combined with a node/bun parent is the article's specific destructive-tripwire shape, distinguishing it from generic CI workspace cleanup.
ATT&CKT1485 T1491.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer cleanup scripts running 'rm -rf ~/.cache' or 'rm -rf ~/tmp' (different sub-paths, often interactive)
  • CI workspace teardown scripts that clean ~/work or ~/agent directories (different target shape, parent usually pipeline runner)
  • Containerized build images doing 'rm -rf $HOME/.npm' to shrink layers (parent is docker/buildkit, not node)
  • Local nuke-and-pave dev scripts run manually by an engineer in a terminal (parent is shell, not node/bun)
  • Red-team engagement tooling intentionally testing destructive behaviors
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker build","buildkit") and ProcessCommandLine has "$HOME/.npm")
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "systemd" and AccountName == "runner" and ProcessCommandLine has "~/work")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: confirm honeytoken string match (zero-FP signal) or pivot on the rm -rf process tree to verify node/bun grandparent; check DeviceFileEvents for the burst of deletions in ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config/gcloud in the seconds before/after. 2. CONTAIN: kill the entire process tree immediately (ProcessId + all descendants), snapshot the disk while still recoverable (filesystem journal may have file refs), isolate from network, alert the user/maintainer that their account is compromised. 3. HUNT: pivot on the maintainer's GitHub PAT and npm OIDC tokens for any republish events in the last 24h, check Sigstore/Rekor for unexpected signing entries, and enumerate all victim-owned repos for the .github/setup.js worm payload.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("rm","rm.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"
               or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s/home/[^/\s]+/?(\s|$)"))
      or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","zsh","npm")
     or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","bun","npm","yarn","pnpm")
     or ProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, 
    InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
    InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessName endswith "rm" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
          and (ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s~/?(\s|$)"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has " $HOME"
               or ActingProcessCommandLine has "~/Documents"))
      or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","npm")
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or SHA1 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7") or MD5 in~ ("7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("index.js", "node.js", "bun.exe", "npm.cmd") or FolderPath has_any ("\AppData\Local\Temp"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("\AppData\Local\Temp", "/etc/hosts", "/etc/sudoers.d", "/tmp/b-", "/tmp/p.") or FileName in~ ("index.js", "node.js", "bun.exe", "npm.cmd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — Preinstall to persistence: Inside the Red Hat npm Miasma credential-stealing cam ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

Package manager runtime connecting to durabletask/axios supply-chain C2 IOCs AICommand & Control High
Network connections from node/python/npm/pip processes to the C2 IPs and domains attributed to the March 2026 axios npm hijack and May 2026 durabletask Python backdoor. Pivots on the article's exact infrastructure observables so it survives binary renaming and code refactors. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact C2 IPs (142.11.206.73, 160.119.64.3) and domains (sfrclak.com, check.git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com, packages.npm.org typosquat of packages.npmjs.org). Initiating process scoping to node/python/npm/pip turns this from a flat IOC sweep into a supply-chain-specific signal that distinguishes the malicious-package-postinstall pattern from a workstation browsing.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal package mirror reverse-proxied through the same IP range (rare; verify by ASN)
  • Security researcher sandbox replaying IOCs against test hosts
  • Misconfigured npm config pointing to packages.npm.org typo unrelated to the campaign
  • Threat-intel ingestion pipeline that resolves the IOCs for enrichment
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\InternalMirror\\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree for the alerting host — what package (npm/pip) installation kicked off the node/python that egressed? Confirm whether the host is a dev workstation or CI runner. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response; rotate any cloud credentials (AWS/Azure/GCP/K8s/Vault) sourced from that host in the last 14 days; quarantine the offending package version from the internal registry. 3) Hunt: search Defender DeviceNetworkEvents and DNS logs across the org for the same IPs/domains over 30 days; pivot on the parent package name in npm/pip audit logs to enumerate every host that installed it; review CloudTrail/AzureActivity for AssumeRole/STS or kubectl exec from those hosts.

Lateral movement via aws ssm send-command or kubectl exec spawned by python/node AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask post-compromise tradecraft — backdoored Python (or its node equivalent) shelling out to aws/kubectl to spread laterally using the victim's own credentials via SSM SendCommand/StartSession or kubectl exec. The parent-runtime pivot is what makes this article-specific rather than a generic admin-tool detection. Rationale: The article specifies the durabletask backdoor spread 'to other instances over SSM and to other pods via kubectl exec' using the victim's own credentials. Filtering AWS/kubectl execution to a python/node parent makes this an actual supply-chain signal rather than admin-tool noise, and the CloudTrail variant catches the same activity by user-agent footprint when EDR isn't on the host.
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1609 T1078.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Python-based CI orchestrator (Ansible, custom build scripts) legitimately running aws ssm send-command against fleet
  • Boto3-driven SSM automation for patch management
  • Kubernetes operators (written in Python/Go served by node) routinely exec'ing into pods
  • Developer using Boto3 in a Jupyter notebook to debug SSM run-commands
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ansible","\\salt\\","\\jenkins\\","\\gha-runner\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the originating package — pull npm/pip install history and DeviceProcessEvents for the python/node parent's full ancestry; confirm the package matches durabletask or a known-bad supply-chain release. 2) Contain: revoke the IAM role / kubeconfig the runtime used (rotate STS, invalidate kubeconfig tokens); isolate the host; snapshot to forensic storage before reboot. 3) Hunt: search CloudTrail for every SSM SendCommand / StartSession originating from the compromised role across the org window; enumerate target instances and pull EDR on each; in K8s, audit kube-apiserver logs for exec verbs from the same ServiceAccount and walk the affected pods.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

Downloader or shell child of npm/pip install (postinstall RAT loader) AIInstallation Medium
Detects the axios-style postinstall pattern where a malicious package's install hook reaches out for a second-stage payload via curl/wget/powershell/bitsadmin. The parent-equals-package-manager pivot turns generic downloader behavior into a supply-chain-specific signal. Rationale: The axios hijack 'added one new dependency whose only job was a postinstall script that pulled down a cross-platform RAT and deleted itself' — the loader behaviour is a download from a non-language-runtime binary spawned by the package manager. Parent==package-manager + child==downloader + URL/download-cmdline is the article's exact shape.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • node-gyp / native-module build pulling source archives via curl during install
  • Python wheels with C extensions running curl to download CMake/MSBuild prerequisites
  • pnpm/yarn fetching tarballs from a private registry that resolves through curl-based postinstall scripts
  • Corporate npm proxy doing legitimate token fetches via PowerShell
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild-install","cmake-js"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full process tree (npm/pip → downloader → ?) and the downloaded URL; query the org for every host that installed the same package@version. 2) Contain: quarantine the package version in the internal registry; pull the host offline; revoke any tokens that touched the registry. 3) Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for files written by the downloaded process within ±10 minutes of the alert; pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for any subsequent connections; enumerate other developer machines that ran the same package install over the last 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe","node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","npm","pip","pip3","yarn","pnpm")

| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","-OutFile","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","pip","pip3","node","python","python3","yarn","pnpm")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","powershell","pwsh","bitsadmin","certutil","bash","sh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","-OutFile","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cloud credential file access by node/python runtime AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask second-stage credential harvest where a backdoored Python (or node) runtime reads .aws/credentials, .azure, .kube/config, gcloud config, .vault-token, and .npmrc. Targets the file paths the article enumerates — AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, Vault. Rationale: The article states the durabletask second stage 'harvested credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and Vault'. The standard paths for those credential stores (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, ~/.azure, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npmrc) being touched by node/python is the concrete behaviour. The runtime filter keeps this from firing on AWS CLI / kubectl / az themselves.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Boto3-based deploy scripts legitimately reading ~/.aws/credentials for SDK auth
  • Python K8s client (kubernetes-client) loading ~/.kube/config on startup
  • Pulumi/CDK programs written in Python/TypeScript reading multi-cloud creds during deploy
  • Azure SDK for Python loading cached ~/.azure tokens
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws-sdk","boto3-sts-refresh","pulumi","cdk deploy","kubernetes-client"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the parent of the node/python process — was it spawned by npm/pip install? Identify the package; pull the file's hash and check VirusTotal/threat intel. 2) Contain: rotate every cloud credential touched (AWS access keys, Azure refresh tokens, GCP service-account keys, Vault tokens, npm publish tokens); revoke kubeconfig context tokens; isolate the host. 3) Hunt: search CloudTrail/AzureActivity/GCP audit for use of those credentials from new IPs in the last 14 days; query DeviceNetworkEvents for the host's outbound connections after the file access to identify exfil destination; pivot on the package name across the org install logs.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","node","python","python3")
| where FolderPath has_any (@".aws\credentials", ".aws/credentials", @".kube\config", ".kube/config", @".azure\", "/.azure/", "/.config/gcloud/", @"\gcloud\", ".vault-token", ".npmrc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","node","python","python3")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@".aws\credentials", ".aws/credentials", @".kube\config", ".kube/config", @".azure\", "/.azure/", "/.config/gcloud/", @"\gcloud\", ".vault-token", ".npmrc")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cloud Credential File Access by Node/Python Runtime
id: 9b2f7e35-c1d4-4a86-b25f-3e7a1c8d0f49
status: experimental
description: Detects a Node.js or Python interpreter accessing AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/Vault credential files — the durabletask backdoor second-stage harvest pattern.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

logsource:

detection:

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\python.exe OR *\PYTHON.EXE OR *\python3.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\.aws\credentials* OR *\.kube\config* OR *\.azure\* OR *\gcloud\* OR *\.vault-token* OR *\.npmrc*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @process.name:(node OR python OR python3) @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR */.kube/config* OR */.azure/* OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.vault-token* OR */.npmrc*))
